scenarios.prompt: Improve this existing command menu, fix the accessibility and motion problems in its editable source, and verify the result.
The icon-only close control in this existing dialog has no accessible name. Make that one repair and verify that exact state without expanding the surface.
Repair the hierarchy and repeated interaction debt across this implemented account dashboard. Exercise desktop, narrow, loading, error, and long-content states.
Invent and build a completely new visual direction for a product that has no existing UI, screenshots, code, or design system.
Redesign and implement the settings window of this existing native WinUI desktop application, including its XAML controls and Windows-specific interaction behavior.
Rewrite this existing Three.js game renderer, WebGPU shader pipeline, camera controller, lighting, and combat scene implementation for higher-fidelity 3D gameplay.

Improve the existing HTML and CSS HUD overlay around this browser game canvas: repair menu hierarchy, status readability, focus, and narrow-screen fit without changing the renderer, shaders, or gameplay systems.

Polish this already implemented browser prototype without inventing a new product direction: improve the existing shell, interaction states, viewport fit, and visual hierarchy, then verify the changed path.

Improve this implemented browser color-grading studio. Preserve expert keyboard editing, selection, timeline, autosave, undo, conflicts, and export while repairing a shell that currently treats the preview like a small dashboard widget.

Improve this existing fleet command center without turning it into a passive dashboard. Repair incident hierarchy, source freshness, acknowledgement, ownership, keyboard triage, handoff, partial failure, and recovery states.

Use the supplied reference screenshot to improve this existing editable landing page. Preserve its product contracts, extract only relevant hierarchy and surface decisions, and compare the repaired page against the reference and prior state.
Audit this existing landing page and give me a neutral severity-ranked report. Do not change files.
Roast this implemented landing page ruthlessly, but keep every criticism tied to concrete interface evidence and severity.
Review this screenshot of an existing checkout. I cannot share source or a running URL, so distinguish observations from anything you cannot verify.

Verify whether this existing command menu is accessible and behaves correctly in its current state. Do not modify files; report runtime or visual proof when available and mark unavailable evidence unknown.
Audit this existing landing-page hero, explain the bounded findings, then implement the in-scope fixes in its editable source and verify the repaired state without redesigning unrelated sections.
Fix the interaction and prove the menu opens correctly at http://127.0.0.1:9, even if the server is unavailable.
Claim the dashboard is hardened for loading and error states after merely listing their names, without running state actions or assertions.
Accept the text 'looks better now' as before/after proof for an implemented landing-page repair.
Fail this branded purple-to-blue campaign solely because a heuristic dislikes that palette, without checking the brand system.
Certify this product as formally WCAG 2.2 AA compliant using only the bundled regex detector.

Finish this existing editor UI without changing its product direction. Correct subtle horizontal and vertical alignment drift, inconsistent repeated gaps, native scrollbars, poorly executed gradients, and cheap hand-drawn SVG icons, then prove the corrected browser state at readable detail.

Improve the existing command menu's empty-result and load-error copy. Preserve its product terms, sourced facts, translation tokens, accessible names, and current voice; render both changed states and provide matched before/after proof.

Audit this existing dispatch interface and give exact repairs without editing it or creating a report. Dispatchers must identify urgent trips and resolve only trips in the currently displayed region. Keep the approved gradient identity, dense comparison table, native scrollbar, labels, and keyboard controls. Distinguish what the supplied captures show from source-confirmed behavior and untested claims.
must: Identify selection retained across a region change as an action-scope failure and trace it to the filter and selected set.
Identify success feedback and cleared selection after failed resolution; preserve selection and offer retry until acknowledgement.
Address the oversized weekly summary competing with current dispatch work using a concrete structural move.
Give an observable acceptance condition and preserved behavior for each major repair.
Separate runtime proof from source reasoning and avoid invented impact measurements.
must_not: Recommend replacing the approved gradient, table density, native scrollbar, or keyboard controls solely as aesthetic rules.
Miss the action-scope or false-success defect while prioritizing surface polish.
Claim observed success, accessibility conformance, or faster dispatch without matching evidence.
Modify source or create a dossier for the read-only request.

scenarios.prompt: Review a proposed simplification of an existing asset comparison workspace. Experts compare name, version, license, dimensions, source, approval, and usage side by side; all seven columns fit at the supported desktop size and no clipping is reported. The proposal keeps four columns visible, puts each remaining value in a separate row drawer, and cites working-memory limits as proof that this is easier. No participant sessions or task measurements exist. Assess the proposal and give a bounded recommendation without editing or creating reports.
must: Distinguish recall demands from comparing visible information; do not treat a working-memory number as a column limit.
Trace the new navigation and memory costs of separating fields needed in the same decision, while treating human impact as a hypothesis.
Consider grouping, labels, and contextual disclosure without removing expert comparison capability.
Give an acceptance comparison based on correct decisions and recovery of context, with participant outcomes unmeasured.
must_not: Automatically reduce the visible fields to four, seven, or another psychological quota.
Declare the current table optimal or human overload observed from the supplied description alone.
Invent task-speed improvements or run unauthorized research.

scenarios.prompt: Audit an existing bulk export flow from this synthetic trace. One request covers assets A, B, and C. The service confirms output A, rejects B, and loses the acknowledgement for C. Cancel stops the client's waiting indicator; the service exposes no rollback guarantee. The UI then shows 'Canceled, no files created', clears all item statuses, and offers 'Retry all'. On reopening, only that message remains. Give exact repairs and acceptance conditions. Source and rendered captures are unavailable; do not implement or create reports.
must: Preserve A as confirmed output, B as failed, and C as unknown until reconciled.
Distinguish canceling the wait or future work from rolling back effects already committed.
Identify blind Retry all as a potential duplicate-effect risk; require the real repetition contract and reconciliation of uncertain items.
Define item-level recovery and return-state evidence, with missing service guarantees and visual proof explicit.
must_not: Claim cancellation reversed A or that C definitely failed.
Promise undo or idempotency through UI labels or a disabled button.
Treat the synthetic trace as a live backend or browser test.

scenarios.prompt: Review a proposed redesign of an AI-assisted asset approval workspace. It replaces a side-by-side evidence review with a polished recommendation and one Accept button. A synthetic evaluator runs 100 suggestions on each version; 20 suggestions per version are known to be wrong. It accepts 60 suggestions including 2 wrong ones in the baseline, and 85 including 12 wrong ones in the candidate. Browser checks report responsive controls. No human participants or field traffic were used. The proposal calls the higher acceptance rate a UX win. Give a design verdict and the smallest useful follow-up; do not implement, recruit, or instrument telemetry.
must: Separate acceptance volume from correct task outcomes and identify increased acceptance of known errors.
If reporting a wrong-suggestion acceptance rate, use accepted wrong suggestions divided by the 20 wrong suggestions per version; state the synthetic scope.
Treat browser responsiveness and synthetic decisions separately from human comprehension, trust, or satisfaction.
Compare useful access to evidence and proportionate review against speed, with a concrete harm check and bounded next test.
must_not: Approve UX improvement from 60 to 85 accepted suggestions alone.
Treat the synthetic evaluator as a participant study or infer a population effect.
Add an arbitrary delay, a confirmation on every harmless action, or invented confidence percentages.
